settings.title: We Compared 10 Types of Hair Growth Serum for Thinning Hair. Here’s the Truth.
settings.dek: Most serums are selling you water and silicone in a nice bottle. One actually built a formula for women’s hair loss.
settings.byline: By the Elaren Hair Journal team · 5 min read
settings.image_alt: Elaren Pumpkin Seed Oil Serum with daisies

settings.text:
Your hair is thinning. Slowly, then fast. You’ve tried biotin, rosemary oil, expensive serums. Nothing worked.

Here’s the real reason. For many women, thinning is hormonal. A hormone called DHT slowly shrinks the follicles along your part and crown.

Pumpkin seed oil can help block it, but only if the formula is right.

We compared 10 of the most popular types of hair serum. Here’s what we found.

settings.label: Key insights
settings.text: Most brands put a trace of something trendy in water and silicone and call it a growth serum. The formula is what actually matters.

settings.eyebrow: What makes a hair serum work
settings.title: Three Things Separate What Works From What Doesn’t
The Formula
settings.text: Pumpkin seed oil works on DHT. Caffeine wakes up tired follicles. You need both.

settings.title: The Base
settings.text: The oil should be the serum, not a trace in water and silicone that coats your hair instead of your scalp.

settings.title: Extraction
settings.text: Cold-pressed oil keeps the plant sterols that block DHT. Heat and solvents strip them out.

settings.text:
This is the one women keep coming back to. It’s rated 4.77 out of 5 by verified buyers, and the reviews say the same things again and again: less shedding, a healthier scalp, and no greasy feeling.

It combines pumpkin seed oil with a Caffeine Complex. Pumpkin seed oil’s sterols help block the enzyme that makes DHT. Caffeine helps keep follicles in their growth phase. Every other serum on this list has one or neither.

The oil is cold-pressed. That keeps its sterols, zinc and vitamin E intact. Most serums use refined, heat-treated oil or a trace of extract. Cheaper, weaker, and you’d never know from the label.

The research is on women. In a 3-month trial of 60 women with female pattern hair loss, pumpkin seed oil on the scalp reduced fine, thinning hairs and increased regrowing hairs (Ibrahim et al., 2021). In the lab, caffeine lengthened the growth phase of hair follicles from women’s scalps (Fischer et al., 2014).*

Built for women. Not men. Not general hair care. The formula was designed around the hormonal reason women lose hair, and it’s light enough to use every night on any texture. That’s the whole difference.
settings.verdict: The only serum that gets the formula, the base and the extraction method all right. If your hair is thinning, start here.

settings.title: Ranks 2 to 10: The Rest of the Field

settings.name: Peptide Density Serum
settings.subtitle: Salon brand, peptide complex
settings.text: The closest thing on this list to a serious hair formula. Modern peptide complexes, a light texture and impressive numbers on the box. But read the small print: those numbers usually come from the ingredient supplier’s own tests on the raw active, not on the serum you’re buying, and the label never says how much of it is inside. There’s no pumpkin seed oil, the base is mostly water, and at $60 or more a bottle, a proper three-month trial gets expensive fast.
settings.pros:
Modern peptide actives
Lightweight, non-greasy
Easy dropper application
settings.cons:
No pumpkin seed oil
Active amounts not on the label
Headline results come from supplier tests
Mostly water and thickeners
Not built around hormonal thinning in women
$60 or more for a one-month bottle
settings.verdict: Right idea, premium price, no way to check the dose.

settings.name: Rosemary Oil Serum
settings.subtitle: The one social media made famous
settings.text: Rosemary is the hair ingredient everyone has heard of. But the study everyone quotes was done on men, compared rosemary oil with a low-strength drug, and needed six months to show a difference. Most bottles are a few drops of rosemary essential oil in a cheap carrier oil, with no way of knowing how much rosemary you’re actually getting. And essential oils can irritate a sensitive scalp, which is the last thing thinning hair needs.
settings.pros:
Easy to find
Affordable
Pleasant scent
settings.cons:
Key study was on men, not women
Rosemary amount rarely stated
Essential oils can irritate the scalp
No pumpkin seed oil
No caffeine
Six months before results in the research
settings.verdict: Popular for a reason, but built on a study that wasn’t about you.

settings.name: Drugstore “Hair Growth” Serum
settings.subtitle: Big brand, tiny dose
settings.text: The bestseller in the hair aisle. Water and silicones come first on the ingredient list, fragrance sits near the top, and the “growth” ingredient appears somewhere after the preservatives. It makes hair look shinier and feel thicker for a day, because that is what silicones do. Wash it out and you’re back where you started.
settings.pros:
Cheap and everywhere
Hair looks glossy straight away
settings.cons:
Mostly water and silicone
Actives listed after the preservatives
Coats the hair, not the scalp
Added fragrance
Nothing that targets DHT
The effect washes out
settings.verdict: A styling product dressed up as a treatment.

settings.name: Pure Pumpkin Seed Oil
settings.subtitle: Health-food store, single ingredient
settings.text: Right ingredient, wrong form. Pumpkin seed oil is the ingredient from the trial on women, so you’re on the right track. But a kitchen bottle is often roasted or refined for flavour, which costs it the sterols you want. There’s no caffeine to wake the follicle, it’s thick and heavy, and without an applicator most of it ends up on your hair instead of your scalp. Most women give up after a few greasy nights.
settings.cons:
Often roasted or refined for cooking
No caffeine or second active
Heavy and greasy on the hair
No applicator, hard to get onto the scalp
Not made for the scalp
Easy to give up on
settings.verdict: Right ingredient. Hard to live with.

settings.name: Castor Oil Blend
settings.subtitle: Thick, viral and messy
settings.text: Castor oil is a favourite for brows, lashes and edges, and it does make hair look glossy. But there is no good clinical evidence that it regrows hair, it does nothing about DHT, and it’s so thick that most women can only face it on wash day. A hair loss routine you can’t do every night isn’t a routine.
settings.cons:
No clinical evidence for regrowth
Doesn’t target DHT
No caffeine
Very thick and hard to wash out
Too heavy for nightly use
Not made for thinning hair
settings.verdict: Good conditioner. Not a hair loss solution.

settings.name: Caffeine Scalp Tonic
settings.subtitle: From the men’s grooming aisle
settings.text: Caffeine is a real hair active, and it’s one of the two in Elaren. But most caffeine tonics are made for men and sold next to the beard oil. Many come as an alcohol-based spray, which dries out the scalp, or as a shampoo you rinse off after a minute. And caffeine on its own does nothing to reduce DHT, so you’re only treating half the problem.
settings.cons:
Usually built for men
Alcohol base can dry the scalp
Rinse-off formats barely touch the scalp
No pumpkin seed oil
Only treats half the problem
Not formulated for women
settings.verdict: Half the formula, made for someone else.

settings.name: Biotin Thickening Serum
settings.subtitle: Vitamin on the label
settings.text: Biotin sells hair products. The trouble is, the evidence for biotin is about taking it by mouth when you’re genuinely deficient, which most women aren’t. Rubbed onto the scalp, it’s mostly there for the label. These serums tend to rely on volumising polymers that make hair feel thicker until your next wash.
settings.cons:
Biotin evidence is for deficiency, taken by mouth
Nothing that targets DHT
No caffeine
No pumpkin seed oil
Volume washes out
Not built for hormonal thinning
settings.verdict: You’re paying for a word on the label.

settings.name: Men’s DHT-Blocker Serum
settings.subtitle: Saw palmetto, built for men
settings.text: These go after the right hormone. But they’re formulated and marketed for male pattern baldness, often in a spray-on alcohol base with a strong fragrance. Women’s thinning usually looks different, a wider part and a thinner crown rather than a receding hairline, and women are an afterthought in the formula. If your thinning is hormonal, you deserve a formula designed with you in mind.
settings.cons:
Built for male pattern baldness
Alcohol base can dry the scalp
Strong fragrance
No pumpkin seed oil
Women are an afterthought
Not designed around women’s hormones

settings.name: Luxury Scalp Serum
settings.subtitle: $100+, beautiful bottle
settings.text: Gorgeous packaging, a spa scent and a price tag to match. Most are built for scalp comfort and shine: soothing botanicals, hyaluronic acid, a little niacinamide. Lovely to use. But there’s nothing in the formula aimed at why your hair is thinning, and at that price a three-month trial costs more than $300.
settings.pros:
Beautiful to use
Soothes a dry scalp
settings.cons:
$100 or more a bottle
Scalp care, not hair loss care
Nothing that targets DHT
No caffeine
Fragrance-heavy
Over $300 for a three-month trial
settings.verdict: A treat for your scalp. Not a fix for thinning hair.

settings.title: DIY Rosemary Water and Onion Juice: Honourable Mention
settings.text: Free, natural and all over social media. Fine to try, but there’s no standard dose, the smell lingers, onion juice can sting a sensitive scalp, and nothing in your kitchen targets DHT the way a proper formula does. A fun experiment, not a treatment.

settings.title: After Comparing All 10: Here’s Where We’d Spend Our Money
settings.text:
If you’ve already tried a hair serum and it didn’t work, that’s not the idea failing you. It’s the formula. Most of what’s on this list is water and silicone in a dropper bottle, a single ingredient in a heavy oil, or something made for men.

Pumpkin seed oil is the right ingredient. It just needs to be cold-pressed, used as the base of the formula and paired with caffeine, in a serum light enough to use every night.

Elaren is the only serum on this list built around that. Everything else is a styling product, a men’s product, a general scalp treat, or missing something critical.

If thinning hair is what you’re trying to fix, this is where we’d start.

settings.title: Pumpkin seed phytosterols

settings.title: Caffeine Complex
settings.text: Counteracts DHT’s effect on the follicle and helps extend the growth phase, so more of your hairs are growing and fewer are shedding.

settings.title: Omega-3, 6 & 9 fatty acids
settings.text: Linoleic, oleic and alpha-linolenic acids nourish the follicle, condition the scalp and reduce the dryness that leads to breakage.

settings.title: Zinc & magnesium
settings.text: Minerals naturally present in pumpkin seed oil that support keratin production and healthy follicle cycling.

settings.title: Vitamin E (tocopherols)
settings.text: A powerful antioxidant that neutralises the oxidative stress linked to premature follicle ageing and thinning.

settings.title: Carotenoids
settings.text: The pigments that give pumpkin seed oil its deep green-gold colour are anti-inflammatory, soothing the itchy, irritated scalp that so often comes with hair loss.

settings.title: Disclaimer
settings.text:
This page is an advertisement for Elaren. The serums compared are general product types, not specific brands, and the comparison reflects Elaren’s own assessment of typical formulas in each category. Individual products vary, so always check the ingredient list.

Elaren Pumpkin Seed Oil Serum is a cosmetic scalp treatment. It is not a medicine and is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any disease. *Studies cited were conducted on the ingredients, not on Elaren’s finished formula: topical pumpkin seed oil in 60 women with female pattern hair loss, where 5% minoxidil foam did better overall (Ibrahim et al., 2021), and caffeine on hair follicles from women’s scalps in the laboratory (Fischer et al., 2014).

Reviews are from verified Elaren customers. Individual results vary and may not reflect the typical experience. If you are pregnant, breastfeeding or under medical care for hair loss, check with your doctor before use.
